ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=5\mathrm{kg}$ is pushed by a horizontal force $F$ and remains stationary on a rough fixed inclined plane. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the plane is $\mu=0.25$. The maximum static friction is equal to the kinetic friction. Find: ($\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$, $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$) (The result can be expressed as a fraction)

1. How large should the force $F$ be for the object to experience no friction?
2. When an object is at rest on an inclined plane, the range of possible values for the force $F$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the rough inclined plane is fixed on the horizontal ground, and the inclined plane slopes upward to the right, with the angle of inclination marked as θ. The block is placed on the inclined plane, and the horizontal external force F pushes the block from left to right. Since F is horizontally to the right, and the inclined plane rises to the right, F has an upward component F cosθ along the inclined plane, and also has a normal component F sinθ pressing toward the inclined plane. Then reason: Take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction, and outward perpendicular to the inclined plane as the positive direction. It is known that m=5 kg, g=10 m/s^2, so mg=50 N; sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, μ=0.25. Equilibrium in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane: the supporting force N is jointly determined by the perpendicular component of gravity and the component of the horizontal force pressing toward the inclined plane, therefore N=mg cosθ+F sinθ=50×0.8+0.6F=40+0.6F. Along the inclined plane direction, the horizontal pushing force component is F cosθ=0.8F, and the downhill component of gravity is mg sinθ=50×0.6=30 N. If f is used to denote the algebraic value of the static friction force, then the equilibrium condition can be written as F cosθ-mg sinθ+f=0, so f=mg sinθ-F cosθ=30-0.8F. 1. When the block is not subject to friction, f=0, therefore 30-0.8F=0, giving F=30/0.8=37.5 N. 2. When the block is at rest, the magnitude of the required static friction force cannot exceed the maximum static friction force: |f|≤μN, that is |30-0.8F|≤0.25(40+0.6F)=10+0.15F. Solve the inequality: 30-0.8F≤10+0.15F, giving 20≤0.95F, so F≥400/19 N; at the same time 30-0.8F≥-(10+0.15F), giving 40≥0.65F, so F≤800/13 N. Therefore when at rest, the range of F is 400/19 N≤F≤800/13 N.

raw_record.question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=5\mathrm{kg}$ is pushed by a horizontal force $F$ and remains stationary on a rough fixed inclined plane. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the plane is $\mu=0.25$. The maximum static friction is equal to the kinetic friction. Find: ($\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos 37^{\circ}=0.8$, $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$; results may be expressed as fractions.)

1. How large should the force $F$ be for the object to experience no friction?
2. When the object is at rest on the inclined plane, what is the range of possible values of $F$?

method.method_draft: Use direct force resolution along axes parallel and perpendicular to the incline. From the image, note that the block sits on a plane rising to the right and the applied force F is horizontal to the right, so F has an up-slope component F cosθ and an inward-normal component F sinθ. From the text, use m=5 kg, g=10 m/s^2, θ=37°, sinθ=0.6, cosθ=0.8, and μ=0.25 with maximum static friction μN. Perpendicular equilibrium gives N=mg cosθ+F sinθ. Parallel equilibrium gives F cosθ - mg sinθ + f=0, so the required static friction is f=mg sinθ-F cosθ. For no friction set f=0, giving F=mg sinθ/cosθ. For rest impose |mg sinθ-F cosθ|≤μ(mg cosθ+F sinθ), then solve the two linear inequalities for the interval of F.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中粗糙斜面固定在水平地面上，斜面向右上方倾斜，倾角标为 θ。物块放在斜面上，水平外力 F 从左向右推物块。由于 F 是水平向右的，而斜面向右上升，所以 F 沿斜面有向上的分量 F cosθ，并且有压向斜面的法向分量 F sinθ。

再推理：取沿斜面向上为正方向、垂直斜面向外为正方向。已知 m=5 kg，g=10 m/s^2，所以 mg=50 N；sin37°=0.6，cos37°=0.8，μ=0.25。

垂直斜面方向平衡：支持力 N 由重力垂直分量和水平力压向斜面的分量共同决定，因此 N=mg cosθ+F sinθ=50×0.8+0.6F=40+0.6F。

沿斜面方向，水平推力分量为 F cosθ=0.8F，重力下滑分量为 mg sinθ=50×0.6=30 N。若用 f 表示静摩擦力的代数量，则平衡条件可写为 F cosθ-mg sinθ+f=0，所以 f=mg sinθ-F cosθ=30-0.8F。

1. 物块不受摩擦时 f=0，因此 30-0.8F=0，得 F=30/0.8=37.5 N。

2. 物块静止时，所需静摩擦力大小不能超过最大静摩擦力：|f|≤μN，即 |30-0.8F|≤0.25(40+0.6F)=10+0.15F。
解不等式：30-0.8F≤10+0.15F，得 20≤0.95F，所以 F≥400/19 N；同时 30-0.8F≥-(10+0.15F)，得 40≥0.65F，所以 F≤800/13 N。因此静止时 F 的范围为 400/19 N≤F≤800/13 N。

method.method_draft: Use a resultant-force/friction-cone viewpoint. From the image, identify the contact plane orientation and that the non-contact applied forces are gravity downward and F horizontally rightward. From the text, take the numerical values and μ=0.25. Combine gravity and the horizontal push into one external resultant. Decompose this resultant relative to the plane: tangential drive T=F cosθ-mg sinθ and compressive normal drive C=mg cosθ+F sinθ. For no friction, the external resultant must be exactly normal to the plane, so T=0. For static equilibrium with friction, the contact reaction must lie within the friction cone, equivalently |T|/C≤μ. Substitute sin37=0.6, cos37=0.8, mg=50 N, and solve |0.8F-30|≤0.25(40+0.6F).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个物块放在固定斜面上，斜面从左下向右上倾斜，斜面与水平面的夹角标为 θ。物块受到一个从左向右的水平推力 F。接触面是斜面，非接触力包括竖直向下的重力和水平向右的推力 F。

推理：按合力/摩擦锥方法，把重力 mg 和水平推力 F 合成为外力，再沿斜面方向和垂直斜面方向分解。取沿斜面向上为正，则切向驱动力 T=F cosθ-mg sinθ；压紧斜面的法向驱动力 C=mg cosθ+F sinθ。已知 m=5 kg，g=10 m/s²，所以 mg=50 N；sin37°=0.6，cos37°=0.8。

1. 无摩擦时，外力合力必须正好沿斜面法线方向，即 T=0：
F cos37°-mg sin37°=0，
0.8F-50×0.6=0，
0.8F=30，
F=37.5 N。

2. 静止时，接触反力必须在摩擦锥内，即 |T|≤μC：
|F cos37°-mg sin37°|≤0.25(mg cos37°+F sin37°)，
|0.8F-30|≤0.25(40+0.6F)，
|0.8F-30|≤10+0.15F。
展开为双边不等式：
-(10+0.15F)≤0.8F-30≤10+0.15F。
左边给出：0.8F-30≥-10-0.15F，所以0.95F≥20，F≥400/19 N。
右边给出：0.8F-30≤10+0.15F，所以0.65F≤40，F≤800/13 N。
因此静止时 F 的范围为 400/19 N≤F≤800/13 N。

method.method_draft: Use limiting impending-motion cases to find the two endpoints, then include all F values between them. From the image, F pushes horizontally right, so increasing F tends to drive the block up the slope, while too small F lets gravity tend to pull it down the slope. From the text, use m=5 kg, g=10 m/s^2, θ=37°, sinθ=0.6, cosθ=0.8, and μ=0.25. First find the no-friction value by balancing only the up-slope component of F with the down-slope component of weight: F cosθ=mg sinθ. For the lower endpoint, assume the block is just about to slide down, so friction is maximal and up the plane: F cosθ+μN=mg sinθ with N=mg cosθ+F sinθ. For the upper endpoint, assume the block is just about to slide up, so friction is maximal and down the plane: F cosθ=mg sinθ+μN with the same N. Solve these two endpoint equations and state the allowable rest range between them.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个粗糙固定斜面，斜面向右上方倾斜，倾角标为 θ；物块放在斜面上；一个水平向右的力 F 作用在物块上。水平向右的 F 沿斜面方向的分量指向斜面上方，因此增大 F 会使物块有上滑趋势；F 还会把物块压向斜面，使支持力增大。

推理：取沿斜面向上为正方向，垂直斜面向外为正方向。已知 m=5 kg，g=10 m/s^2，所以 mg=50 N；sin37°=0.6，cos37°=0.8，μ=0.25。

水平力 F 的沿斜面分量为 F cosθ，方向沿斜面向上；重力沿斜面分量为 mg sinθ，方向沿斜面向下。水平力 F 垂直斜面方向的分量压向斜面，因此支持力 N=mg cosθ+F sinθ。

1. 无摩擦时，沿斜面方向平衡：F cosθ=mg sinθ。代入数值：0.8F=50×0.6=30，所以 F=30/0.8=37.5 N。

2. 静止时摩擦力大小不能超过最大静摩擦力 μN。下限对应物块将要下滑，摩擦力沿斜面向上：F cosθ+μN=mg sinθ，且 N=mg cosθ+F sinθ。代入：0.8F+0.25(50×0.8+0.6F)=50×0.6，即 0.8F+0.25(40+0.6F)=30，0.8F+10+0.15F=30，0.95F=20，F=400/19 N。

上限对应物块将要上滑，摩擦力沿斜面向下：F cosθ=mg sinθ+μN。代入：0.8F=30+0.25(40+0.6F)，即 0.8F=30+10+0.15F，0.65F=40，F=800/13 N。

因此物块能静止时，F 的取值范围为 400/19 N ≤ F ≤ 800/13 N。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m=5\mathrm{kg}$ is pushed by a horizontal force $F$ and remains stationary on a rough fixed inclined plane. The angle of inclination of the plane is $37^{\circ}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the plane is $\mu=0.25$. The maximum static friction is equal to the kinetic friction. Find: ($\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos 37^{\circ}=0.8$, $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$; results may be expressed as fractions.)

1. How large should the force $F$ be for the object to experience no friction?
2. When the object is at rest on the inclined plane, what is the range of possible values of $F$?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the rough inclined plane is fixed on the horizontal ground, and the inclined plane slopes upward to the right, with the angle of inclination marked as θ. The block is placed on the inclined plane, and the horizontal external force F pushes the block from left to right. Since F is horizontally to the right, and the inclined plane rises to the right, F has an upward component F cosθ along the inclined plane, and also has a normal component F sinθ pressing toward the inclined plane.

Then reason: Take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction, and outward perpendicular to the inclined plane as the positive direction. It is known that m=5 kg, g=10 m/s^2, so mg=50 N; sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, μ=0.25.

Equilibrium in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane: the supporting force N is jointly determined by the perpendicular component of gravity and the component of the horizontal force pressing toward the inclined plane, therefore N=mg cosθ+F sinθ=50×0.8+0.6F=40+0.6F.

Along the inclined plane direction, the horizontal pushing force component is F cosθ=0.8F, and the downhill component of gravity is mg sinθ=50×0.6=30 N. If f is used to denote the algebraic value of the static friction force, then the equilibrium condition can be written as F cosθ-mg sinθ+f=0, so f=mg sinθ-F cosθ=30-0.8F.

1. When the block is not subject to friction, f=0, therefore 30-0.8F=0, giving F=30/0.8=37.5 N.

2. When the block is at rest, the magnitude of the required static friction force cannot exceed the maximum static friction force: |f|≤μN, that is |30-0.8F|≤0.25(40+0.6F)=10+0.15F.
Solve the inequality: 30-0.8F≤10+0.15F, giving 20≤0.95F, so F≥400/19 N; at the same time 30-0.8F≥-(10+0.15F), giving 40≥0.65F, so F≤800/13 N. Therefore when at rest, the range of F is 400/19 N≤F≤800/13 N.
